newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco says environment damage costs $2.3 bln/year.
newsitem.headline: Morocco says environment damage costs $2.3 bln/year.

text.p: Damage to the environment costs Morocco the equivalent of $2.3 billion a year or 8.0 percent of its gross domestic product, a Moroccan minister said on Monday.

"Certain studies show that degradation of the environment costs Morocco nearly 20 billion dirhams a year, or 8.0 percent of GDP. If nothing is done to halt this damage, its incidence may accelerate and affect the country's development in future," Mohamed Hama, Minister of Economic Encouragement, said.
Hama, whose address was reported by the official news agency MAP, was talking to delegates at a regional meeting in Rabat attended by North African and World Bank experts.

Morocco, which registered average economic growth of four percent in the last two decades "should improve its economic performance and solve its structural problems including environment issues," he said.
Hama did not say what caused the pollution and environment degradation but experts say the main cause is "the edible oil industry in Casablanca and Meknes, and leather industry in Fes".
Meknes and Fes are located in central Moroccan provinces.
King Hassan set up a ministry of environment -- for the first time-- in August 1992 but with no significant means to carry out its duties, a World Bank expert has said.
In recent years, Morocco launched a media campaign aimed at educating the country's 27 million people about the dangers of air and water pollution.

"These problems cannot be solved unless an integrated development policy on the long term is drawn up to guarantee a balance between the needs for growth and the necessity of preserving Morocco's future," the minister said.
The meeting, which is expected to end on Tuesday, was seen by experts as part of Morocco's continuing campaign to attract international funds to help it solve its increasing environmental problems.
